configs.description: Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. The 10 slot bays are EMPTY; fabric, rp are populated. Enough to power on and reach the box, which is the question most people ask first and the one `default` used to answer with whatever the drawing happened to be populated with.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: Cisco publishes no chassis-level power draw for any ASR 9000. Table 14's "Power Dissipation" row says only "Use the Cisco Power Calculator ... to estimate the maximum power distribution", so the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Recorded in provenance as no-chassis-power-figure since the family was modelled; scoped here so a comparison can tell this apart from a figure nobody has looked for
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level maximum and typical draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the Power Calculator is the only answer the vendor will give

gaps.note: NARROWED BY THE ASR 9000 CARD STANDARD, NOT CLOSED. The line card bays here were once grown to meet a component - 42.67 thick to fit a9k-4hg-flex and 403.10 long to fit the 5th-generation envelope - and the RP bays to 46.0 to fit a supervisor data sheet. None of those numbers is used now: all 19 card bays are 41.4 x 395.7 with a 41.4 x 355.6 opening, per asr9000-card-standard in provenance. Two of the three standard figures are sourced: 395.7 is the fourth-generation "includes ejector bracket/lever" envelope, and 355.6 is the Table A-10 plate length, 0.65 mm from the ASR 9010 cage and 1.75 / 2.55 mm under the two cages measured here. THE THICKNESS IS NOT. 41.4 is the figure Cisco states most often, chosen so every card in the family is one envelope; the original-generation cards are stated at 43.7 and the RSP-880 at 46.0, and both are drawn at 41.4 by decision. A fit check between a bay and a card is now satisfied by construction, so it can no longer catch a wrong thickness - which is why this stays open.
gaps.wanted: a caliper reading of an ASR 9000 card thickness (still requested on roc-ops/Portrayal#16), or a dimensioned figure of the clear opening of any ASR 9000 card cage, which would confirm or move 41.4

gaps.note: cisco/a99-sfc3@1 carries power-draw-max-w 340, and that figure is the ASR 9922's. Table 23 of b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf lists the SAME part number twice with different figures scoped by chassis - "A99-SFC3 Card (ASR 9922)" at 320/330/340 W across the three ambients, and a separate ASR 9912 row at a lower number. These are two scopes rather than two answers: the same card draws less in this chassis than in the 9922. A chassis total built from the component here is therefore CONSERVATIVE - it over-counts each of the seven fabric cards - which is the safe direction but is not the right number. The component cannot carry both without a chassis-scoped mechanism, which the library does not have; casa/c100g records the same species of problem for paired modules.
gaps.wanted: a per-chassis power scope on a component contract, or a separate PID for the 9912 variant

gaps.note: Three power shelves are drawn as single openings rather than four module openings each. Figure 23 numbers them M0 to M3 per shelf and Table 15 gives "Version 2 power system: Up to twelve AC power modules per system, four per tray" - so twelve, and the count is not in doubt. The boundaries are: the master draws all three shelves populated, so scanning returns module detail rather than separators. The shelves' vertical extents here are estimated from the band below the RP/FC cage rather than measured off separator rules, which is weaker than everything else in this file and is why they are cutouts and not bays.
gaps.wanted: a figure showing the power shelves empty, or a dimensioned front elevation

gaps.note: THE BOTTOM IS THE ONLY FACE OF THIS CHASSIS WITH NO SOURCE, and it is not a gap in this file's research. There is no bottom view of ANY ASR 9000 chassis anywhere in the 78-document intake: every figure caption in all 65 PDFs was searched for "Bottom View", "underside" and "bottom of the chassis", and the result is zero hits. That is a fact about how Cisco documents a rack chassis rather than about this model - a face that sits on rack rails and is never serviced gets no figure. The face is SIZED correctly from Table 13, so a rack elevation and the 3D box are the right shape; what it lacks is any statement of what is on it. Nothing is invented to fill it, and no region is added naming the absence, because a check passed by annotating that you have nothing is worse than a check failed honestly. THIS HOLDS THE CHASSIS AT CAPABILITY 2. Front, rear, top, left and right all now carry sourced content; the bottom alone does not, and level 3's implementation requires content on all six. The written design asks only that six faces be "present, sized, and mutually consistent", which this file satisfies - the content requirement comes from `_has_content`, which was written for level 1. See docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.
gaps.wanted: a bottom elevation, a photograph of the underside, or a way for a view to declare itself deliberately empty so that empty-by-verification counts where empty-by-omission does not

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices

air-filter.note: datasheet - Table 17, b-asr9k-hardware-installation-guide.pdf p228: "Cisco ASR 9912 Router - Three air filters on the front of the RP and FC card cage". THREE filters, on the FRONT, which is unlike every other chassis in the family - the 9006 and 9904 put theirs on the right side and the 9010, 9906 and 9910 underneath a cage. Not modelled as bays; no figure dimensions them

airflow.note: datasheet - "Cisco ASR 9912 Router: Front-to-rear cooling path. The inlet is at the bottom front of the chassis, and the exhaust is at the upper rear", b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf p3740

asr9000-card-standard.note: all 19 card bays here - ten line card slots, two RP and seven FC positions - are the ASR 9000 card standard: size 41.4 x 395.7 and a visible opening of 41.4 x 355.6, POSITIONED on the measured rail centres, each keeping the centre it had. The 2.66 mm between 41.4 and the 44.06 pitch is the card guide between slots, chassis structure rather than bay. 395.7 is the ejector-inclusive figure of the fourth-generation line card data sheets, and a lab reading of a real A9K-RSP880 agrees (roc-ops/Portrayal#16). 41.4 is the thickness Cisco states most often, 1.63 in, and is NOT MEASURED; the line card bays were 42.67 and the RP bays 46.0, and both now draw at 41.4 as a deliberate standard rather than a correction. 355.6 is Table A-10, the card plate at 14 in. The cages here measure 357.35 (line cards) and 358.15 (RP and FC) tall off the stencil; those stay as the cutouts, and the standard draws 355.6

bottom-face.note: datasheet - the bottom is NOT featureless after all, and the feature is the one thing every footprint figure dimensions. Figure 14 dimensions 22 in (55.88 cm) from the rear. The rack mounting flange is a vertical plate spanning the chassis height, so it intersects the BOTTOM plane as well as the top and appears on this face as a line across the width at that depth. That is a real dimensioned feature rather than an annotation of absence, which is the distinction that matters here - an earlier revision of this file said the bottom was unreachable without inventing something, and that was wrong. What remains true is that no BOTTOM VIEW of any ASR 9000 chassis exists in the 78-document intake; what this face carries is a feature dimensioned in a TOP-down figure whose geometry the bottom necessarily shares. Positions are given from the REAR, which is how the figures dimension them

calibration.note: measured - gate 1 passed. Calibrating x on 482.6 mm (the 19.0 in rack face) and y on Table 13's 1333.5 mm independently gives 0.20134 and 0.20144 mm/px, agreeing to 0.05 percent

card-compatibility.note: datasheet - the per-card datasheets carry a "Chassis compatibility" row. c78-743580, the 5th Generation High-Density Multi-Rate data sheet, says of A9K-20HG-FLEX-SE/-TR and A9K-8HG-FLEX-SE/-TR: "Compatible with the Cisco ASR 9006, ASR 9010, ASR 9904, ASR 9906, ASR 9910, ASR 9912, and ASR 9922 chassis". This chassis is named, so those four are in every line card bay. Cards whose rows omit the 9912 are deliberately absent. A9K-400G-DWDM-TR joins the ten line card slots on the same footing: c78-736456 names this chassis, and it was kept out only because it was drawn at 43.7 against a 42.67 bay. Under the card standard both are 41.4, so the size objection is gone and the compatibility row decides

card-envelope-headroom.note: derived - 439.21 mm of clear vertical space between the structure above this card cage and the structure below it, measured off this chassis's own committed geometry. Any card envelope larger than that cannot be installed regardless of what its data sheet states. It was once a check on the 428 mm control-card lengths; no card or slot uses that figure any more, and the 395.7 standard sits well inside it. Not a source for the bays

card-orientation.note: datasheet - stated directly, and it had been an inference until now. The Overview and Reference Guide's "Chassis Slots" section (b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf p17) names every chassis in the family and gives the ejector position as the tell: on the ASR 9912 every RP, FC and LC faces the front and stands vertically, with ejector levers and captive screws at the card's top and bottom. A bay therefore places a card component unrotated. Only the ASR 9006 and ASR 9904 are horizontal; the 9010, 9906, 9910, 9912 and 9922 all stand their cards up, including the 21 RU 9010. This section supersedes the three-way inference an earlier revision rested on - the slot figures, Figure 2's "four on each side" callout and the measured cage aspect - all of which agreed with it.

chassis.note: datasheet - Table 13, b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf p130. ASR 9912: chassis height 52.5 inches (133.4 cm), chassis width 17.6 inches (44.7 cm) with "19.0 inches (48.3 cm) including chassis rack-mount flanges and front doors", chassis depth 25.7 inches (65.2 cm), "29.4 inches (74.7 cm) including the cable management system" and "30.1 inches (76.4 cm) including cable management system and front doors". Modelled as the BODY, 447.0 x 1333.5 x 652.0 mm, taking the bare depth. This row gives 17.6 and 19.0 on separate lines, which is what showed the ASR 9910's row has its flange phrase attached to the wrong number

compliance.note: datasheet - data_sheet_c78-501767.pdf series compliance list, transcribed as printed

electrical.note: datasheet - Table 15 (AC) and Table 16 (DC), pp132-135, ASR 9912 columns only

environmental.note: datasheet - Table 14, p131. The 9912 is in the narrower short-term group, 23 to 122 degF (-5 to 50 degC), with the 9010, 9910 and 9922

fabric-and-rp.note: datasheet - the seven FC positions accept cisco/a99-sfc3@1, which Table 23 names as an ASR 9912 part in its own right. The two RP positions accept the RP3 pair; the ASR 9900 Series Route Processor 3 data sheet is the source for the part and Figure 23 for the positions. THE FABRIC CARD'S POWER FIGURE IS SCOPED AND MUST NOT BE READ OFF THE COMPONENT HERE - see gaps

first-generation-fabric-accepted.note: datasheet - the fabric bays gain this chassis's first-generation switch fabric card, placed on the component's own attrs.chassis, which names exactly one chassis. That single-chassis declaration is why it can be added without a compatibility row: the part says where it goes

four-hg-flex-accepted.note: datasheet - the A9K-4HG-FLEX and A99-4HG-FLEX pairs added to the line card slots, and each is placed on ITS OWN declared chassis list rather than on an inference from generation. The A9K pair's contract names all seven chassis; the A99 pair's names five - "ASR 9922, ASR 9912, ASR 9910, ASR 9906 and ASR 9904" - so the two are not interchangeable even though they share an envelope. A component that declares what it fits is a better source than a chassis deciding what it will take

four-port-100ge.note: datasheet - c78-740092's "Chassis compatibility" row: "Compatible with the Cisco ASR 9006, ASR 9010, ASR 9904, ASR 9906, ASR 9910, ASR 9912, and ASR 9922 chassis". All seven, stated outright, and the component's own attrs.chassis carries the same list. At 41.4 mm it fits every line card bay in the family. Added to the line card slots only - a compatibility row names a chassis, not a slot, and this chassis's RSP and RP positions take supervisors

grounding.note: datasheet - "Bottom rear right side of the chassis", b-asr9k-hardware-installation-guide.pdf p125, illustrated by Figure 137

lifecycle.note: datasheet - searched. No end-of-sale or end-of-life notice for this chassis was found

master-faces-verified.note: drawing - checked deliberately, because Cisco's ASR 9910 masters are SWAPPED and modelling from a filename there would build the chassis inside out. The 9912's are correctly named: asr-9912-ac-front carries the cable management tray with the cisco logo, both card cages and the populated power shelves, while asr-9912-ac-rear carries the two fan trays, a block of yellow warning labels and the power inlets. Figure 23 corroborates by marking the fan trays "(rear insertion)"

modular-line-card-support.note: datasheet - the ten line card slots, 0 to 9, take the ASR 9000 400G and 200G modular line cards (A9K-MOD400-SE, -TR and A9K-MOD200-SE, -TR). The data sheet c78-735809 names this chassis twice: p4, Features and benefits, and p6, Table 2, Chassis compatibility, which lists the ASR 9912 among seven routers. Table 2 (p7) gives the ASR 9912 a maximum of 10 of these cards, and this chassis has 10 line card slots. The route processor bays are not line card slots and do not take them. The A9K-MOD80 and A9K-MOD160 are not in that data sheet and are not added here. Added for roc-ops/Portrayal#885

no-chassis-power-figure.note: NOTE, and NARROWED. The current Table 14 says only to use the Cisco Power Calculator, so there is no chassis-level figure for THIS chassis in any document held, and the module total here is a floor. That is narrower than what an earlier revision of this file claimed: it said Cisco publishes no chassis draw for ANY ASR 9000, and that is false. The older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide (asr9kELCIGbk.pdf, OL-17500-09) states "Power Dissipation 7600 W maximum (Cisco ASR 9010 Router)" and 4556 W maximum for the ASR 9006 in its Table A-1 - a table the current revision deleted. Those two chassis predate this one and no equivalent figure for this model appears in either revision, so this is the vendor being silent about this chassis rather than about the family

pitch-against-the-siblings.note: NOTE - 44.06 here against 43.78 measured the same way on the ASR 9910 and 43.75 on the ASR 9906. The 0.28 mm difference is larger than either chassis's own label spread, so it is probably real rather than noise, and it is consistent with the 9912 and 9922 being a slightly different mechanical build from the 9906 and 9910 - they take the full-width A99-SFC3 fabric card at 41.4 mm where the 9910 takes the double-width A99-SFC3-S at 76.2. Recorded rather than averaged away

power-shelves-derived-from-a-neighbour.note: DERIVED, not measured, and the derivation is better than the estimate it replaces. The three shelves were placed by eye at y 1125, 1195 and 1265 because the master draws them populated and no separator rule is readable. That estimate put shelf-0 ELEVEN MILLIMETRES INSIDE the RP bay: the RP/FC cage ends at 1117.36 and an RP bay carries 18.77 mm of ejector past it, so nothing can begin above 1136.13. That is a constraint from a part with nothing to do with power. Three shelves then fill 1136.13 to the chassis bottom at 1333.50 - 197.37 mm, 65.79 each - and are placed at 1136.50, 1202.17 and 1267.84 on a 65.67 pitch at 63.0 tall, which leaves a visible gap between them and lands the last edge 0.66 mm short of the chassis bottom. THE TWO DECIMAL PLACES ARE ARITHMETIC AND NOT PRECISION. The underlying inputs are a measured cage edge and a published ejector allowance; nothing in any figure resolves a power shelf to a hundredth of a millimetre. Read them as "three shelves evenly filling the space the RP bay leaves", which is what they are

ru.note: datasheet - 52.5 in / 1.75 = exactly 30.00 RU, and the stencil's height_in of 5.2500 agrees exactly. One of the four chassis in the family where the guide and the stencil need no reconciling

side-and-top-faces.note: datasheet - NAMED but not dimensioned, and drawn as regions rather than decor for that reason. Figure 14 (the chassis footprint figure in b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf) shows the top plate outline and the rack mounting brackets, and Figure 77 (the chassis cooling path side view) shows the airflow through the side. Both name what is on those faces; NEITHER dimensions any feature on them, so nothing here carries coordinates. Contrast the ASR 9906, whose HIG Figure 17 gives explicit rail positions at 9.45 in and 5.00 in from the rear and where those rails ARE drawn. The distinction is deliberate: a region says "this is here" and decor says "this is here, at this size, in this place", and only the second needs a dimension behind it

side-face-labels-say-when-a-position-is-.note: every region on a side face now states either where the feature sits or that no figure dimensions it. That second half is the point. A region reading only "Vertical rack rail locations" is silent about position, and silence is indistinguishable from a position that was known and not written down - which is exactly how a feature ends up drawn at the wrong end with nothing to contradict it. casa-cards found seven such features across two chassis where the LABEL WAS RIGHT AND THE GEOMETRY WAS WRONG, and lint stayed green because no rule compares the two. Saying "present but not dimensioned" gives a reader the same thing a distance would: a claim to check the drawing against

slot-pitch-measured-from-the-card-guide-.note: measured - CORRECTED. An earlier revision of this file said both cages PRINT their positions. They do not: what was measured is the row of bolt heads on each cage's card guide rail, checked by eye at 2400 px after the same reading was found to be wrong on the ASR 9910. The numbers are unchanged, because a uniform rail is a better ruler than printed text - a label's centre moves with its character count, and on the 9910 the text row gives pitches ranging 41.78 to 55.16 where its rail gives 43.78 with a spread of 0.2. Ten line card rail bolts centre at 25.08 through 421.61 mm with nine pitches of 44.10, 43.99, 44.09, 44.09, 43.99, 44.10, 44.09, 43.99 and 44.09 - a mean of 44.06 with a spread of 0.11 mm. The nine RP/FC positions give the same 44.05, so the two cages share a pitch, which is what makes a fabric card and a line card the same mechanical slot here. Both cages measure 6.36 to 440.24 mm across the body. THE SIBLING CONFIRMS IT: the ASR 9922's front master, measured the same way, gives 44.06 with a spread of 0.11 - identical, and the two are the same build

slots.note: datasheet - Figure 23 "Cisco ASR 9912 Router Slot Numbering", p38 of b-asr9k-overview-reference-guide.pdf, read at 250 dpi. Top to bottom: fan trays FT0 over FT1 marked "rear insertion"; then Slot 0 to Slot 9 carrying LC0 to LC9; then a second cage of nine positions labelled by NAME and not by slot number - RP0, FC0, FC1, FC2, FC3, FC4, FC5, FC6, RP1; then power shelves PS0, PS1, PS2 each M0 to M3. The RP/FC positions are named directly by Cisco, so they are named directly here rather than given invented slot numbers

strip-is-centred-on-the-plane.note: the rack mounting strip is 3.9 mm thick and is placed so the DIMENSIONED PLANE PASSES THROUGH ITS MIDDLE, at y = plane - 1.95. Neither edge carries the number. An earlier revision put the plane on one edge, which meant the figure's dimension was 3.9 mm from where the drawing said it was, and which edge differed between chassis - casa-cards found the same inconsistency across the two it owns and centred them the same way

strip-label-carries-the-number.note: the region label states the figure's own dimension AND its conversion to a distance from the front. That is not decoration: it is the only number in the file a reader can check the geometry against, and its absence is why the ASR 9906's strips sat in the wrong half of the box through two reviews before a human noticed. Where the label carried a distance - on the ASR 9006 and 9904 - the same error was caught in minutes

top-and-bottom-agree.note: the rack mounting flange is one vertical plate, so it intersects the top and bottom planes at the SAME depth and appears on both faces at the same y. An earlier revision drew it only on the bottom, which left the two faces of one chassis disagreeing about where the chassis bolts to the rack - the kind of internal inconsistency this work has spent the night finding in other people's artefacts. casa-cards' ASR 9006 and 9904 match across both faces and are the standard this follows

top-and-bottom-view-convention.note: ON THIS CHASSIS'S TOP AND BOTTOM VIEWS, y = 0 IS THE REAR AND y = depth IS THE FRONT. Verified on this chassis's own footprint figure rather than carried across from a sibling: the figure prints "Rear of chassis" above the drawing and "Front of chassis" below it, read by eye because that text is vector art and does not extract. Stated here because it is not derivable from the file and because reading it the other way turns every depth-wise position into its complement - which is exactly the error that put this family's ASR 9906 strips in the wrong half of the box.

twelve-port-100ge.note: datasheet - c78-737623's "Chassis compatibility" row reads "Compatible with the Cisco ASR 9904, ASR 9910, ASR 9912, and ASR 9922 chassis". This chassis is named, so cisco/a99-12x100ge@1 joins the line card bays. NOTE WHICH CHASSIS IS ABSENT: the ASR 9906. That card goes in every other 9900-generation chassis and not in the 9906, which is the second time a Cisco compatibility row has singled that chassis out, and exactly why these lists are transcribed rather than inferred from generation

weight.note: datasheet - Table 13. "Chassis only - 181 pounds (82.10 kg)" and "Chassis: fully configured using all card slots and three power trays - 643 pounds (291.66 kg)"
